svg.title: Open proposals: one real proposal the policy objected to twice, and what the record kept
svg.desc: Five numbered steps of one real proposal, MiniMax on 2026-10-12. One: the model proposes to trim 20 shares if the price rebounds above 225 within one session, and forecasts with probability 0.55 that it closes under 213 on the fifth session. Two: code reviews it on three channels; facts and feasibility can refuse it and did not, the strategy channel can only object and objected twice: a sale without an escalated event, an active move without a catalyst. Three: of the four outcomes the record keeps, published, published over an objection, refused and unpublished, this one was published with its objections attached. Four: the record is read on two separate axes; its payoff is not triggered, because the price never traded above 225, and its forecast is scored on its own. Five: a comparison of three arms, old policy, observations only and policy reference, frozen before it starts, with first records on 2026-10-13. Nothing is promoted and no order is placed.

text.tspan: A different strategy can still be a valid proposal.
One real proposal, MiniMax · 00100, 2026-10-12: the registered policy objected twice. It was still filed.
Its own hypothesis and method, as written.
02 · CODE REVIEWS IT ON THREE CHANNELS
Two can refuse it. One can only object.
objected 2 times: the registered policy disagrees
Refused and unpublished proposals still count
Each record freezes the method text, forecast, inputs and review. Revisions append; nothing is rewritten.
Payoff and being right, scored apart
A call can be right and still lose money, so neither
score stands in for the other.
A comparison frozen before it starts
A missing mark stays a hole.
Evidence for human review: no automatic method promotion, sizing or order placement.
